newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZFOE to launch electricity futures on November 18.
newsitem.headline: NZFOE to launch electricity futures on November 18.

text.p: The New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange on Tuesday said it proposed to launch electricity futures contracts on November 18, 1996.
The NZFOE said the launch would make it the first exchange in the world to introduce cash-settled electricity futures contracts.
Six one-month contracts will initially be available for trading.

"The decision to launch electricity futures is in response to demand from participants of the NZ wholesale electricity market for a means to hedge risk associated with price volatility of the spot electricity market," NZFOE said in a statement.

It said the deregulation of the wholesale electricity industry and growing competition between buyers and sellers of wholesale electricity were significant factors in the growing demand for risk management products.
The contracts will be cash-settled, meaning any still open after the last day of trading will be valued against a mandatory settlement price.
"There is no provision for physical delivery of electricity as the intention of the contract is to allow management of price or financial risk associated with the supply of electricity," NZFOE said.

Trading would take place on NZFOE's existing computerised network, linking its authorised dealers in Auckland, Wellington and Sydney. Trading hours are Monday to Friday 1.30 p.m. to 4.30 p.m. NZ time.
